page: Microsoft Azure L4as_v5 is a storage-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD x86_64 processor providing 4 dedicated vCPUs. It includes 32.0 GB of system memory, delivering an allocation of 8.0 GB of RAM per virtual CPU core. This instance type does not contain hardware GPU accelerators and does not bundle complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

A key component of the L4as_v5 hardware architecture is its dedicated local storage subsystem. The instance comes equipped with a 960 GB local NVMe SSD, engineered for low-latency disk operations and high sequential throughput. Additionally, the instance is capable of attaching Azure Premium Storage to support workloads that require managed persistent disk volumes alongside the fast local disk tier.

From an architectural efficiency perspective, the 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio paired with fast local NVMe flash offers an efficient profile for I/O-bound services that do not need large processor pools. However, because local NVMe disk arrays are ephemeral in cloud environments, workloads must handle replication or snapshots to avoid data loss during host maintenance. Compute-heavy operations needing more than 4 vCPUs will face processing constraints on this instance tier.

The L4as_v5 instance is appropriate for transactional and NoSQL databases, search engine indexing, in-memory caches requiring fast local persistence, data warehousing nodes, and logging pipelines that require high disk throughput and moderate compute resources.
description: Microsoft Azure L4as_v5 is a storage-optimized virtual machine featuring 4 dedicated AMD x86_64 vCPUs and 32.0 GB of system memory. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance provides an 8.0 GB memory-to-core ratio and integrates a dedicated 960 GB local NVMe SSD to deliver high-throughput, low-latency disk operations. It also supports Azure Premium Storage for managed persistent disks, while excluding GPU hardware and complimentary public IPv4 allocations. The architecture emphasizes local storage bandwidth and substantial memory capacity relative to core count. Because the bundled NVMe disk is ephemeral, reliable operation relies on software replication or managed disk backups. This profile is engineered for transactional databases, NoSQL datastores, distributed caching layers, and search indexing services requiring fast local read and write operations.
